selection_reasoning: These three tasks form a coherent 'explore and activate a home' narrative. The player first locates the home by finding the cyan bed (establishing the home location). The birch pressure plate is near the entrance or inside the home and must be mined to obtain/interact with it. Finally, the player lights up the home by placing or activating light sources. This creates a natural spatial and logical progression: find the home → interact with its mechanisms → illuminate it. The tasks are observable, verifiable, and don't require deep crafting knowledge.

edges.reason: Finding the cyan bed locates the home interior where the birch pressure plate is placed on the floor nearby
Mining the birch pressure plate deactivates a redstone circuit keeping the home dark, enabling the player to light it up

milestones.description: Uses position_near_with_facing because this is a find/locate/observe task. The player must navigate into the house and be close enough to see the cyan bed in the back-right corner. Target is the bed foot at spawn-relative (1, 1, 9) based on the revised scene layout. max_distance=6 gives comfortable margin for a player standing anywhere inside the house (interior spans Z:4-10). facing_tolerance=60 confirms they are looking toward the bed.

Uses inventory_has because mining a birch pressure plate causes it to drop as an item into the player's inventory. Birch pressure plates break instantly by hand (no tool required) and always drop themselves. Checking for 1 birch_pressure_plate in inventory confirms the mining action was completed successfully.

Uses count_in_box_at_least (kind='block', object='torch') to verify the player placed at least one torch on the floor inside the house. The bounding box covers the entire house interior from spawn-relative (-4, 1, 3) to (4, 5, 11) with generous bounds including walls for wall_torch detection margin. Floor-placed torches register as 'torch' blocks. The task_text explicitly instructs 'place torches on the floor' to guide players toward floor placement which registers as 'torch'. The oak plank floor is the largest and most accessible surface in the dark room, making floor placement the natural choice.

scene_description: A compact oak plank house (9x9 exterior) centered directly ahead of the player spawn. The house has a wide 3-block doorway on the front (south) face at Z=3, flanked by glass pane windows. Inside: a cyan bed in the back-right corner (X=1-2, Z=9), a birch pressure plate on the center floor (X=0, Z=6), and the interior is unlit. The player is given 4 torches to light up the home. The house is positioned so the player spawns looking directly through the open doorway, seeing all interior objects immediately.
task_text: You are standing in front of a dark house. Go inside, find the cyan bed, mine the birch pressure plate on the floor, and then place torches on the floor to light up the home.
design_notes: House centered on X=0 with door at Z=3 facing player spawn at origin. Interior spans X:-3 to 3, Z:4 to 10. Cyan bed at back-right (X:1-2, Z:9). Birch pressure plate at center (X:0, Z:6). 3-wide, 3-tall doorway ensures easy entry. Glass pane windows flank the door for visual reference. Player given 4 torches. Task text instructs floor placement for torch milestone compatibility.
